[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#executive-summary]

## Executive Summary

This standard defines **recommended** practices for implementing event transformation capabilities in .NET 8 applications. Event transformation includes mapping between event schemas, enriching events with domain data, filtering and routing based on business rules, and aggregating multiple events. While integration event consumption (STD-APP-INT-001) and publishing (STD-APP-INT-002) are mandatory, this standard provides guidance for optional transformation scenarios where platform-level transformation is insufficient or requires domain-specific logic.
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#key-recommendations]

### Key Recommendations

- **AutoMapper 12.0+** for declarative event-to-event mapping with custom resolvers
- **FluentValidation 11.9+** for transformation validation and business rule enforcement
- **Domain Enrichment** from repositories/services with caching for performance
- **Filtering & Routing** using specification pattern for business rule-based routing
- **Stateful Aggregation** with Redis or Streamiz.Kafka.Net for windowed operations
- **Transformation Pipelines** with composable ITransformer implementations
- **OpenTelemetry 1.7+** instrumentation for transformation monitoring
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#when-to-apply-transformations]

### When to Apply Transformations

Use application-level transformation when:
- Transformation requires domain knowledge or business logic
- Need to query domain data for enrichment (customer details, reference data)
- Complex validation against business rules
- Transformation logic is specific to one application/bounded context

Use platform-level transformation (see STD-INFRA-INT-003) when:
- Transformation is stateless and generic (format conversion)
- High-throughput stream processing without domain logic
- Transformation applies to multiple applications
- Simple mapping/filtering without domain service access

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#purpose]

### Purpose

This standard provides recommended guidance for implementing event transformation logic in .NET 8 applications. It addresses mapping, enrichment, filtering, aggregation, and business logic transformation patterns within application code, distinguishing application-level transformation from platform-level stream processing.
page_texts.9:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope**:
- Application-level event transformation (.NET 8 code)
- Event mapping and schema translation
- Event enrichment from domain data
- Event filtering and routing logic
- Event aggregation and correlation
- Business rule application during transformation
- Transformation validation and error handling

**Out of Scope**:
- Platform-level stream processing (see STD-INFRA-INT-003)
- Kafka Streams/ksqlDB transformations (infrastructure)
- AWS Glue ETL jobs (infrastructure)
- Lambda-based transformations (infrastructure)

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#recommended-requirements]

### Recommended Requirements

> **Note**: These requirements are **RECOMMENDED**. Teams should implement transformation logic when domain-specific business rules or enrichment is required. For generic transformations, consider platform-level solutions (STD-INFRA-INT-003).
page_texts.12:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

The following practices are explicitly **prohibited** when implementing event transformations:

- **Synchronous Database Calls Without Caching**: Do not query databases synchronously during transformation without implementing caching. This creates performance bottlenecks and scalability issues.
- **Transformation Logic in Consumers/Publishers**: Do not embed transformation logic directly in consumer or publisher classes. Transformations must be separate, reusable components.
- **Hardcoded Business Rules**: Do not hardcode business rules within transformation code. Use externalized rules engines (NRules) or configuration-based routing for maintainability.
- **Stateful Transformations Without Proper State Management**: Do not implement stateful transformations (aggregation, correlation) using in-memory dictionaries or lists. Use Redis, Kafka state stores, or Streamiz.Kafka.Net.
- **Missing Error Handling**: Do not implement transformations without comprehensive error handling and DLQ publishing. Failed transformations must be recoverable.
- **Transformation Without Validation**: Do not transform events without pre-transformation and post-transformation validation using FluentValidation or equivalent.
page_texts.13:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

**When to Request an Exception**:
- Technology constraints prevent use of recommended libraries (AutoMapper, FluentValidation)
- Legacy system integration requires different transformation patterns
- Performance requirements necessitate bypassing caching layers
- Specific domain logic conflicts with standard transformation patterns

**Exception Request Procedure**:
1. **Document Justification**: Clearly articulate why the standard cannot be followed
2. **Assess Alternatives**: Demonstrate that alternative approaches were evaluated
3. **Define Mitigation**: Specify how risks will be mitigated without standard compliance
4. **Submit Request**: Submit exception request to Architecture Review Board with:
   - Standard requirement being excepted
   - Business/technical justification
   - Risk assessment and mitigation plan
   - Proposed alternative approach
   - Duration of exception (temporary vs permanent)

**Approval Authority**:
- **Temporary Exceptions (<90 days)**: Application Architecture Team Lead
- **Permanent Exceptions**: Architecture Review Board approval required
- **Emergency Exceptions**: CTO approval with retroactive ARB review within 30 days

**Monitoring and Review**:
- Temporary exceptions reviewed monthly for remediation progress
- Permanent exceptions reviewed annually for continued relevance
- All exceptions tracked in compliance management system

#### REQ-INT-004-003: Event Enrichment from Domain Data

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Add contextual domain information to events for downstream consumers

**Requirements**:
- Implement enrichment as separate transformation step after mapping
- Query domain data using repositories/services injected via DI
- Cache frequently accessed enrichment data with sliding expiration
- Handle missing enrichment data gracefully with null checks and defaults
- Log enrichment failures without failing entire transformation
- Support batch enrichment for multiple events to reduce database queries

**Implementation**: See comprehensive enrichment transformer example with caching in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.17:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-004-event-filtering-and-routing]

#### REQ-INT-004-004: Event Filtering and Routing

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Apply business rules to filter and route events to appropriate topics

**Requirements**:
- Use specification pattern for business rule evaluation
- Route events to different topics based on filter criteria
- Log all filtering decisions for audit purposes
- Support dynamic routing rules from configuration or database
- Publish filtered-out events to audit topic (not DLQ)
- Implement fail-open behavior if routing service unavailable

**Implementation**: See specification pattern and routing transformer examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.18:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-005-event-aggregation-and-correlation]

#### REQ-INT-004-005: Event Aggregation and Correlation

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Combine multiple related events into aggregated events for downstream processing

**Requirements**:
- Implement stateful aggregation using Redis or in-memory state stores
- Define correlation keys for event grouping (e.g., PatientId, ClaimNumber)
- Configure aggregation windows (time-based, count-based, or session-based)
- Handle late-arriving events within configurable grace period
- Publish aggregated events when window closes
- Support partial aggregation and timeout handling

**Implementation**: See Redis-based aggregation and session-based aggregation examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.19:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-006-business-rule-application]

#### REQ-INT-004-006: Business Rule Application

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Apply complex business logic during transformation using rules engine

**Requirements**:
- Use NRules >= 4.0.0 for complex business rule evaluation
- Externalize business rules from code when rules change frequently
- Validate transformation results against business invariants
- Log all rule executions and decisions for audit trails
- Support rule versioning and A/B testing of rule changes
- Handle rule execution failures gracefully

**Implementation**: See NRules configuration and business rules transformer examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-007-transformation-validation]

#### REQ-INT-004-007: Transformation Validation

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Ensure transformed events meet schema and business requirements

**Requirements**:
- Use FluentValidation >= 11.9.0 for transformation validation
- Validate against target event schemas before publishing
- Implement pre-transformation and post-transformation validation
- Publish validation failures to error topic (not DLQ)
- Log validation errors with detailed diagnostics
- Support async validation for database checks

**Implementation**: See FluentValidation validators and validation transformer examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.21:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-008-transformation-error-handling]

#### REQ-INT-004-008: Transformation Error Handling

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Handle transformation failures without losing events

**Requirements**:
- Implement try-catch blocks around all transformation logic
- Publish failed transformations to DLQ with error details
- Log transformation exceptions with original event payload
- Support manual retry of failed transformations from DLQ
- Track error rates and alert on threshold breaches
- Implement circuit breaker for dependent services

**Implementation**: See resilient transformer wrapper and circuit breaker examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.22:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-009-transformation-observability]

#### REQ-INT-004-009: Transformation Observability

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Monitor transformation performance and failures

**Requirements**:
- Instrument transformers with OpenTelemetry >= 1.7.0
- Track transformation duration per event type
- Monitor transformation failure rates and error types
- Export transformation metrics to CloudWatch
- Create distributed traces across transformation pipelines
- Alert on transformation SLA breaches

**Implementation**: See OpenTelemetry instrumentation and metrics examples in accompanying code samples.

---
page_texts.23:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#req-int-004-010-streamizkafkanet-for-stateful-transformations]

#### REQ-INT-004-010: Streamiz.Kafka.Net for Stateful Transformations

**Status**: Recommended
**Rationale**: Use Kafka Streams for .NET when stateful transformations exceed application-level capabilities

**Requirements**:
- Use Streamiz.Kafka.Net >= 1.4.0 for stateful stream processing
- Implement KStream/KTable transformations for event processing
- Configure state stores for aggregations and joins
- Handle rebalancing and state recovery automatically
- Use windowed operations for time-based aggregations
- Support exactly-once processing semantics

**Implementation**: See Kafka Streams topology examples for aggregation, joins, and stateful transformation in accompanying code samples.

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#412-documentation-requirements]

### 4.12 Documentation Requirements

The following documentation must be maintained for each transformation implementation:

**1. Transformation Specification Document**
- Source event schema (JSON schema or examples)
- Target event schema (JSON schema or examples)
- Mapping table (source field → target field)
- Business rules applied during transformation
- Enrichment data sources
- Filter criteria
- Performance requirements (throughput, latency)

**2. AutoMapper Profile Documentation**
- Profile class purpose and scope
- Custom resolvers and their logic
- Type converters used
- Before/After map actions
- Special mapping considerations

**3. Business Rules Documentation**
- Rule ID and description
- Rule logic (pseudocode or decision table)
- Rule version and effective date
- Rule owner/approver
- Test scenarios for each rule

**4. Configuration Documentation**
- All configuration keys and their purposes
- Default values and valid ranges
- Environment-specific overrides
- Configuration change procedures

**5. Error Handling Documentation**
- Error types and handling strategies
- Dead letter queue processing procedures
- Retry policies and thresholds
- Escalation procedures
- Recovery procedures

**6. Operational Runbook**
- Deployment procedures
- Configuration update procedures
- Monitoring and alerting setup
- Troubleshooting guide
- Common issues and resolutions
- Performance tuning guidelines

**7. Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)**
- Decisions made during implementation
- Alternatives considered
- Rationale for chosen approach
- Trade-offs and consequences

All documentation must be:
- Stored in the project repository (docs/ or documentation/ folder)
- Version controlled alongside code
- Reviewed during code reviews
- Updated whenever implementation changes
- Linked from README.md

### 5.2 Claim Line Item Aggregation Example

**Scenario**: Aggregate multiple claim line item events into a single aggregated claim.

**Input Events** (arriving over 5-minute window):
```json
{ "claimNumber": "CLM-12345", "lineNumber": 1, "serviceCode": "99213", "amount": 150.00, "totalLineItems": 3 }
{ "claimNumber": "CLM-12345", "lineNumber": 2, "serviceCode": "80053", "amount": 75.00, "totalLineItems": 3 }
{ "claimNumber": "CLM-12345", "lineNumber": 3, "serviceCode": "93000", "amount": 100.00, "totalLineItems": 3 }
```

**Aggregation Logic**:
- Correlation key: `claimNumber`
- Window: 5 minutes tumbling window
- Completion: 3/3 line items received

**Output Aggregated Event**:
```json
{
  "claimNumber": "CLM-12345",
  "lineItems": [
    { "lineNumber": 1, "serviceCode": "99213", "amount": 150.00 },
    { "lineNumber": 2, "serviceCode": "80053", "amount": 75.00 },
    { "lineNumber": 3, "serviceCode": "93000", "amount": 100.00 }
  ],
  "totalAmount": 325.00,
  "isPartialAggregation": false,
  "windowStart": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "windowEnd": "2025-01-15T10:35:00Z",
  "aggregatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:34:15Z"
}
```

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#53-fraud-detection-with-business-rules]

### 5.3 Fraud Detection with Business Rules

**Scenario**: Detect potential fraud using NRules business rules engine.

**Input Claim**:
```json
{
  "claimId": "CLM-12345",
  "patientId": "PAT-9876",
  "serviceCode": "99213",
  "serviceDate": "2025-01-15",
  "amount": 150.00
}
```

**Business Rules Applied**:
1. **Duplicate Claim Rule**: Check for identical claims in last 30 days
2. **High Frequency Rule**: Check if patient has > 10 claims in 30 days
3. **Unusual Pattern Rule**: Check for service codes not typical for patient's condition

**Rule Execution Result**:
```json
{
  "claimId": "CLM-12345",
  "fraudFlags": ["DUPLICATE_CLAIM"],
  "requiresManualReview": true,
  "reviewReason": "Duplicate service code and date detected within 30 days",
  "rulesExecuted": ["DuplicateClaimRule", "HighFrequencyRule"],
  "validatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
}
```

### 5.4 Patient Session Aggregation

**Scenario**: Aggregate patient portal activities into session events.

**Input Activity Events** (over 30-minute session):
```json

{ "patientId": "PAT-9876", "activityType": "VIEW_CLAIMS", "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:05:00Z" }
```

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#55-lessons-learned]

### 5.5 Lessons Learned

**What Worked Well**:
- **AutoMapper** simplified schema mapping with declarative profiles
- **FluentValidation** caught transformation errors before publishing
- **Redis caching** reduced enrichment latency from 250ms to 10ms (96% cache hit rate)
- **Specification pattern** made routing rules testable and composable
- **OpenTelemetry** provided end-to-end visibility across transformation pipeline

**Challenges Encountered**:
- **Late-arriving aggregation events** required grace period configuration (added 1-minute grace)
- **Circuit breaker tuning** needed adjustment (5 failures → 3 failures threshold)
- **Memory cache sizing** caused evictions under load (increased SizeLimit from 500 to 1000)
- **NRules learning curve** steep for complex rule definitions (created rule templates)

**Performance Optimizations**:
- **Batch enrichment** reduced database queries from 1000/sec to 100/sec (10x improvement)
- **Parallel transformer execution** where no dependencies exist (30% latency reduction)
- **Redis pipelining** for aggregation state updates (50% throughput improvement)

**Recommendations**:
- Start with simple transformations (mapping only) and add complexity incrementally
- Use platform-level transformation (Kafka Streams) for high-throughput stateless operations
- Implement circuit breakers for all external dependencies in enrichment
- Monitor transformation latency and set SLA alerts (p95 < 500ms)
- Use feature flags for gradual rollout of new transformation logic

#### Transformation Architecture

- [ ] `ITransformer<TInput, TOutput>` interface defined for all transformers
- [ ] Transformation pipelines support chaining multiple steps
- [ ] Transformers registered in DI container with appropriate lifetimes (Scoped for stateful, Singleton for stateless)
- [ ] Transformation factory implemented for dynamic transformer selection based on event type

#### Event Mapping

- [ ] AutoMapper >= 12.0.0 configured with explicit mapping profiles per bounded context
- [ ] Custom value resolvers implemented for complex calculations or transformations
- [ ] Mapping configuration validated at application startup using `AssertConfigurationIsValid()`
- [ ] Conditional mappings implemented where event types vary (e.g., Professional vs Institutional claims)
page_texts.55:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#event-enrichment]

#### Event Enrichment

- [ ] Enrichment implemented as separate transformation step after mapping
- [ ] Domain data queried through repositories/services (not direct database access)
- [ ] Frequently accessed data cached with appropriate expiration (15-60 minutes sliding)
- [ ] Missing enrichment data handled gracefully without throwing exceptions
- [ ] Batch enrichment implemented for high-throughput scenarios to reduce database queries

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#filtering-and-routing]

#### Filtering and Routing

- [ ] Specification pattern used for filtering logic (not inline conditionals)
- [ ] Routing decisions logged for audit purposes with correlation IDs
- [ ] Dynamic routing rules supported from configuration or database
- [ ] Fail-open behavior implemented if routing service unavailable (default topic)

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#aggregation-and-correlation]

#### Aggregation and Correlation

- [ ] Stateful aggregation implemented with Redis or Kafka state stores (not in-memory for production)
- [ ] Correlation keys defined clearly for event grouping (e.g., ClaimNumber, PatientId)
- [ ] Aggregation windows configured appropriately (time-based, count-based, or session-based)
- [ ] Late-arriving events handled within grace period (typically 1-5 minutes)
- [ ] Partial aggregations published on timeout with `isPartialAggregation` flag
page_texts.58:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#business-rules]

#### Business Rules

- [ ] Complex business logic externalized using NRules >= 4.0.0 (not hard-coded)
- [ ] Rule execution logged for audit trails with rule names and decisions
- [ ] Rule versioning supported for gradual rollouts
- [ ] Rule execution failures handled gracefully without blocking transformation
- [ ] Business invariants validated after rule application
page_texts.59:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#validation]

#### Validation

- [ ] FluentValidation >= 11.9.0 configured for all transformation validation
- [ ] Pre-transformation validation implemented to catch malformed input
- [ ] Post-transformation validation implemented to ensure output schema compliance
- [ ] Validation failures published to error topic (not DLQ)
- [ ] Async validation supported for database lookups (e.g., patient existence checks)
page_texts.60:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#error-handling]

#### Error Handling

- [ ] Try-catch blocks wrap all transformation logic with appropriate exception handling
- [ ] Failed transformations published to DLQ with full context (input, error, stack trace)
- [ ] Transformation exceptions logged with original event payload for debugging
- [ ] Manual retry supported from DLQ with retry consumer
- [ ] Error rates tracked and alerting configured for threshold breaches (>0.1%)
- [ ] Circuit breakers implemented for dependent services (enrichment APIs, databases)
page_texts.61:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#observability]

#### Observability

- [ ] OpenTelemetry >= 1.7.0 instrumentation added to all transformers
- [ ] Transformation duration tracked per event type with histograms
- [ ] Transformation failure rates monitored with counters by error type
- [ ] Distributed traces created across transformation pipelines with correlation IDs
- [ ] Metrics exported to CloudWatch or OTLP collector
- [ ] Alerts configured for transformation SLA breaches (p95 latency, error rate)
page_texts.62:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#stateful-transformations-if-using-streamizkafkanet]

#### Stateful Transformations (if using Streamiz.Kafka.Net)

- [ ] Streamiz.Kafka.Net >= 1.4.0 configured for stateful stream processing
- [ ] KStream/KTable transformations implemented appropriately (stream for events, table for reference data)
- [ ] State stores configured for aggregations and joins with appropriate retention
- [ ] Rebalancing and state recovery handled automatically by framework
- [ ] Exactly-once processing semantics enabled (`ProcessingGuarantee.EXACTLY_ONCE`)
- [ ] State directories configured on persistent storage (not ephemeral containers)
page_texts.63:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#62-architecture-review]

### 6.2 Architecture Review

Submit to Architecture Review Board if:
- **Complex stateful transformations** requiring significant CPU/memory resources (>2 CPU cores or >4GB RAM)
- **Choosing between application-level and platform-level transformation** affecting multiple teams
- **Implementing custom business rules engines** outside NRules or standard patterns
- **Transformations impact multiple applications** or bounded contexts requiring coordination
- **Transformation latency consistently exceeds 500ms** at p95 requiring optimization
- **State stores exceed 100GB** requiring infrastructure capacity planning
page_texts.64:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#63-exception-process]

### 6.3 Exception Process

**Minor Deviations** (no ARB approval required, document in ADR):
- Using alternative mapping library (Mapster, AgileMapper) instead of AutoMapper if well-justified
- Implementing simpler validation without FluentValidation for basic property checks
- Using in-memory caching instead of Redis for small-scale enrichment (<1000 events/sec)
- Omitting business rules engine (NRules) for simple conditional logic (<5 rules)
- Using synchronous transformers for low-throughput scenarios (<100 events/sec)

**Major Deviations** (ARB approval required):
- Not implementing transformation observability (OpenTelemetry instrumentation)
- Using synchronous blocking calls for enrichment without caching or circuit breakers
- Implementing transformations without error handling or DLQ publishing
- Storing critical transformation state in non-durable storage (container file system)
- Implementing custom serialization outside MassTransit/Kafka standards
- Bypassing schema validation for transformed events
page_texts.65:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#64-key-metrics]

### 6.4 Key Metrics

Monitor these transformation metrics and configure alerts:

1. **Transformation Latency**:
   - p50, p95, p99 transformation duration per event type
   - Target: p95 <100ms for mapping-only, <500ms for enrichment, <1s for aggregation
   - Alert: p95 >1000ms sustained for 5 minutes

2. **Transformation Throughput**:
   - Events transformed per second per transformer type
   - Target: Varies by use case (typically 100-10000 events/sec)
   - Alert: Throughput drops >50% from baseline

3. **Transformation Error Rate**:
   - Percentage of transformations failing validation or encountering errors
   - Target: <0.1% (1 error per 1000 transformations)
   - Alert: Error rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes

4. **Enrichment Cache Hit Rate**:
   - Percentage of enrichment data served from cache vs database
   - Target: >90% cache hits for production workloads
   - Alert: Cache hit rate <70% indicating cache sizing or TTL issues

5. **Enrichment Query Duration**:
   - Time to query domain data from repositories
   - Target: p95 <50ms for cached, <200ms for database queries
   - Alert: p95 >500ms indicating database performance issues

6. **Aggregation Completeness**:
   - Percentage of aggregations completed within window (not partial)
   - Target: >95% complete aggregations
   - Alert: <90% complete indicating late-arriving events or window misconfiguration

7. **Aggregation Window Duration**:
   - Actual time from first event to aggregation completion
   - Target: Within configured window + grace period
   - Alert: Aggregations consistently timing out

8. **Rule Execution Time**:
   - Duration of business rule evaluation per event
   - Target: p95 <50ms for rule execution
   - Alert: p95 >200ms indicating complex or inefficient rules

9. **Transformation Memory Usage**:
   - Memory consumed by stateful transformations, caches, and state stores
   - Target: <4GB per transformer instance
   - Alert: Memory >6GB or increasing trend indicating memory leak

10. **DLQ Message Count**:
    - Number of transformation failures requiring manual intervention
    - Target: <10 messages/day in DLQ
    - Alert: >100 messages/day indicating systemic transformation issues

11. **Circuit Breaker Open Events**:
    - Number of circuit breaker activations for enrichment services
    - Target: <5 events/day
    - Alert: >10 events/hour indicating downstream service degradation

12. **Validation Failure Rate**:
    - Percentage of events failing FluentValidation checks
    - Target: <0.5% for production workloads
    - Alert: >2% indicating upstream data quality issues

[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#unit-testing]

#### Unit Testing

- [ ] Each transformer has unit tests covering happy path and error scenarios
- [ ] AutoMapper profiles validated in unit tests
- [ ] FluentValidation validators have comprehensive test coverage
- [ ] Business rules (NRules) tested independently
- [ ] Mock dependencies (repositories, caches) in transformer tests
page_texts.68:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#integration-testing]

#### Integration Testing

- [ ] End-to-end transformation pipeline tested with real dependencies
- [ ] Redis aggregation logic tested with real Redis instance (Testcontainers)
- [ ] MassTransit publishing tested with in-memory test harness
- [ ] Kafka Streams topologies tested with TopologyTestDriver
- [ ] Circuit breaker behavior tested under simulated failures
page_texts.69:
[standards/application/integration/dotnet/STD-APP-INT-004-dotnet-event-transformation.md#performance-testing]

#### Performance Testing

- [ ] Transformation latency benchmarked at expected throughput
- [ ] Cache hit rates validated under realistic load
- [ ] Aggregation window behavior tested with late-arriving events
- [ ] Memory usage profiled for stateful transformations
- [ ] Concurrency testing for parallel transformation execution

### 6.6 Governance Oversight

**Standards Owner**: Enterprise Architecture - Application Standards Team
- Responsible for maintaining and evolving this standard
- Reviews and approves minor updates to transformation patterns
- Conducts annual standard effectiveness reviews
- Provides clarifications and interpretations

**Compliance Manager**: Quality Assurance and Compliance Office
- Monitors organizational compliance with transformation standards
- Tracks compliance metrics and produces quarterly compliance reports
- Conducts random audits of transformation implementations
- Escalates systemic non-compliance issues to Architecture Review Board

**Governance Body**: Architecture Review Board (ARB)
- Provides oversight and policy direction for integration standards
- Approves major deviations and exceptions requiring ARB review (see section 6.3)
- Reviews standard compliance metrics quarterly
- Approves major standard revisions and new transformation patterns

**Subject Matter Experts**: Integration Architecture Community of Practice
- Provides technical guidance and best practices
- Supports development teams with transformation implementation questions
- Contributes transformation patterns and examples
- Participates in standard reviews and updates

**Review Frequency**: This standard shall be reviewed:
- Quarterly: Metrics and compliance assessment by Compliance Manager
- Bi-annually: Technical accuracy review by SMEs and Standards Owner
- Annually: Comprehensive effectiveness review by ARB

- Standards Owner: architecture-standards@company.com

- ARB Requests: arb-requests@company.com
- SME Community: integration-cop@company.com
